subject: English
title: English 5 (PECTAA, SNC 2020)
questions: In 'Getting Started', who did not complete his part of the project on time?
Everyone except Azlan completed their work on time.
How did Ayesha respond to Azlan's behaviour?
She was patient and shared a book with him
Ayesha was patient with Azlan and shared a book to help him finish.
Who is the writer's role model in the lesson 'Patience'?
The writer's role model is Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH), complete in all aspects.
Rasoolullah (PBUH) was called Saadiq and Al-Amin because of his:
He was called Saadiq and Al-Amin for his honest, truthful nature.
Which city did Rasoolullah (PBUH) travel to, to spread the message of Islam, where people pelted him with stones?
In Taif a mob pelted him with pebbles, yet he prayed for them.
Who accompanied Rasoolullah (PBUH) on the journey to Taif?
He was accompanied by Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha.
How did Rasoolullah (PBUH) respond to the people of Taif?
He prayed for them to be guided
Despite being hurt, he prayed that they or their children would accept the right path.
The main moral value taught in Unit 1 is:
The unit 'Patience' shows the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as an example of patience for all mankind.
Letters that are spelt in a word but not pronounced are called:
Silent letters are written but not pronounced, e.g. k in knife, w in write.
In the word 'knife', which letter is silent?
What is the name of the poem in Unit 2 (Be Grateful)?
The dialogue refers to the poem 'Allah Loves Me'.
Where does the poet see Allah in the first line?
The poem begins: 'I see You in the stars'.
What does the poet ask Allah in the last line?
The poem ends 'O Allah! Just love me more!'
According to Maryam, what message does the poem give?
Allah loves us and is always there for us
Maryam says the poem tells us Allah loves us and is always with us in sadness and happiness.
Words starting with a vowel sound take 'an': an umbrella.
Which article is correct: 'He was ___ famous umpire'?
'Famous' begins with a consonant sound, so we use 'a'.
Which expression is used to give an opinion?
Expressions like 'In my opinion' and 'I think' are used to share opinions.
Fatima Jinnah was the younger sister of:
Miss Fatima Jinnah was the younger sister of Quaid-e-Azam.
What was Fatima Jinnah's profession before she joined the Pakistan Movement?
She was a dentist by profession and later gave it up to help her brother.
Which title was given to Fatima Jinnah?
Due to her untiring efforts she got the title 'Maadar-e-Millat'.
Fatima Jinnah formed the Women's Relief Committee, which was later renamed:
The Women's Relief Committee was later renamed 'All Pakistan Women's Association'.
Dr. Ruth Pfau devoted her life to fighting which disease in Pakistan?
Dr. Ruth Pfau, a German doctor and nun, fought leprosy in Pakistan.
Dr. Ruth Pfau is known as:
She is known as the Mother Teresa of Pakistan.
How many leprosy clinics did Dr. Ruth Pfau set up across Pakistan?
She set up 150 leprosy clinics across the country.
Arfa Karim became the world's youngest:
At nine she became the world's youngest Microsoft Certified Professional.
Samina Baig was the first Pakistani woman to climb:
Samina Khayal Baig is the first Pakistani woman to climb Mount Everest.
Samina Baig belongs to Shimshal village in:
She belongs to Shimshal village in Hunza, Gojal, Gilgit-Baltistan.
Where did the writer's grandparents live?
The writer visited grandparents in Swat during the summer vacation.
Why was the writer shocked on reaching the farmhouse?
The grass was burnt and the trees had wilted
There was burnt yellow grass with bushes and the tall trees had wilted.
Why had the farmhouse become neglected?
The gardener who took care of it had passed away due to illness.
How long did it take the children to restore the farmhouse?
They got everything back the way it used to be within a month.
What exciting activity did the children do in Swat Valley?
They rode zip lines from one hill to another.
According to 'Getting Started', trees reduce air pollution by using:
Trees use carbon dioxide and provide humans with oxygen.
In the poem 'Amazing Planet', who is speaking?
The Earth speaks: 'I am your home, but you destroy my skin and bone.'
What does the Earth ask for in the poem?
No more plastic and no more waste
The Earth says, 'No more plastic, and no more waste.'
The main theme of 'Amazing Planet' is:
The poem asks us to stop polluting the Earth, our only home.
When the weather stays the same for a certain period in an area, it becomes a:
Getting Started explains that weather staying for a certain period becomes a season; seasons make up the climate.
Which word begins with a three-consonant cluster?
'Straw' begins with s-t-r, a three-consonant cluster.
Which sentence politely makes a request?
Could I borrow your camera for this trip?
'Could I borrow...?' is a polite way to make a request.
Why did Dr. Haroon visit the school?
To talk about personal hygiene and COVID-19
He came to talk about personal hygiene and raise awareness about COVID-19.
For at least how long should we wash our hands?
Aqsa said we should wash our hands for at least 20 seconds.
What should we do while sneezing?
Wasif said we should cover our face while sneezing.
What should we do before taking any medicine?
Dr. Haroon said tell your elders first; never take medicine unless elders give it.
Which helps to stop the spread of viral diseases, according to Dr. Haroon?
Wearing a mask and physical distancing
He said never forget to wear a mask and keep physical distance.
Which of these keeps us strong and fit?
Dr. Haroon said eating healthy food and drinking clean water keeps us strong and fit.
In 'What Goes Around, Comes Around', where did the frog invite the mouse?
The frog invited the mouse to come and see the wonderful underwater world.
Why did the mouse hesitate to go with the frog?
The mouse said, 'I would love to go with you but I cannot swim.'
How did the frog tie the mouse to himself?
With a rope around the waist
By tying the mouse's foot to his own with a thread
The frog tied the mouse's foot to his own with a piece of thread.
What happened to the mouse in the pond?
The poor mouse drowned while the unkind frog swam about.
Which bird pounced on the floating mouse?
A hawk saw the mouse and pounced upon it, dragging the frog too.
What is the moral of the fable?
Slow and steady wins the race
As you sow, so shall you reap
The moral: As you sow, so shall you reap.
A short story with animal characters that teaches a moral is called a:
A fable is a short story, often with animal characters, that teaches a lesson.
What did Raffay find on the road?
After Mohsin passed by on a bicycle, Raffay saw a wallet lying on the road.
How much money was in the wallet?
He found three thousand rupees in the wallet.
The wallet belonged to his classmate Mohsin.
Which two things that his teacher said made Raffay feel sorry?
Never tell a lie, and return things found unattended
The teacher had said: never tell a lie, and return unattended things to their owner.
What did Raffay finally do with the wallet?
Raffay went to Mohsin's house, told the whole story and handed over the wallet.
What did Mohsin praise Raffay for?
Mohsin thanked Allah and praised Raffay for his honesty.
What is the title of the poem in the unit 'Patriotism'?
The poem in Unit 9 is 'A Nation's Strength'.
According to the poem, what makes a people great and strong?
Men (people) who stand for truth and honour
'Not gold but only men can make a people great and strong.'
Brave men in the poem work while others:
'Brave men who work, while others sleep, who dare while others fly.'
Why do we celebrate Pakistan Day?
To remember the Lahore Resolution of 1940
Pakistan Day remembers the Lahore Resolution of 1940, which proposed a separate Muslim state.
The Lahore Resolution is also called the:
It proposed an independent Muslim state, so it is also called the Pakistan Resolution.
According to 'Getting Started', what makes a nation strong?
Education makes a nation strong by making people learned and skilful.
In 'laughed', the -ed ending is pronounced as:
After k, s, ch, sh, f, p sounds the -ed is pronounced /t/: laughed, asked.
What did Suleman want to buy for Eid-ul-Azha?
Suleman wanted to buy a goat for Eid.
On which date is Eid-ul-Azha celebrated?
Father said Eid-ul-Azha is celebrated on the 10th of Zil-Hajj every year.
Eid-ul-Azha reminds us of the great sacrifice of:
Muslims sacrifice animals to remember the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim and his son Hazrat Ismail.
What do we do with the meat of the sacrificed animal?
Share it among friends, relatives and the poor
We share the meat among friends, relatives and the needy.
When did Suleman and his father go to the cattle market?
Father said they would go to the cattle market on Sunday.
What colour was the goat they bought?
They bought a white goat for Eid.
Why was Sara sad in 'Let's Be Helpful'?
Her father lost his job and could not buy her a new dress
Sara's father lost his job and couldn't buy her a new dress for the fun fair.
What event was the school going to arrange?
The teacher announced the school would arrange a fun fair next month.
Who suggested saving pocket money to buy Sara a dress?
Maheen said, 'We will save our pocket money and buy Sara a new dress.'
How did Sara feel when she opened the gift?
She was surprised and her eyes filled with delight on seeing a new dress.
What is the message of 'Let's Be Helpful'?
Do not go to fun fairs
The lesson says sharing brings happiness; we should take care of each other.
A dictionary lists words in alphabetical order with meanings and syllables.
What is the national animal of Pakistan?
Markhor is the national animal of Pakistan.
Markhor belongs to which animal family?
It belongs to the goat family.
Markhor is considered a symbol of:
It is considered a symbol of bravery and intelligence.
It is known for its long and curly horns.
How long are the horns of a male markhor, nearly?
Horns on males are nearly 63 inches long; on females around 10 inches.
Where is the markhor mostly found?
It is mostly found in Northern Pakistan and the Himalayas.
What is the average lifespan of a markhor?
The average lifespan of a markhor is 10 to 13 years.
Why were markhors killed by hunters in the past?
They were hunted for their meat and horns, used in traditional medicine and as trophies.
What was Hafsa waiting for during the holidays?
Hafsa anxiously waited for the storybooks her mother had ordered.
Who brought the parcel to Hafsa's house?
The postman handed her the parcel with a smile.
What went wrong with the parcel?
The company sent the wrong books
The book company had mistakenly sent some other books.
What did Hafsa's mother decide to do?
Write a complaint to the seller
She wrote a complaint letter to the seller so they could get the right parcel.
What was the subject of the complaint letter?
The way a person's voice rises and falls while speaking is called:
Intonation pattern is the way the voice rises and falls depending on what is said.
What is the title of the poem in Unit 14 (Together We Live)?
The poem in Unit 14 is 'Two Little Kittens'.
When did the two little kittens begin to quarrel?
'Two little kittens, one stormy night, began to quarrel, and then to fight.'
What did the old woman use to sweep the kittens out?
'The old woman took the sweeping broom and swept them both right out of the room.'
How were the kittens when they crept back in?
Wet with snow and cold as ice
They crept in 'all wet with snow and as cold as ice'.
The kittens found it better to lie by the fire than to:
They found it much better to lie by the fire than to quarrel and fight.
What is the main idea of 'Two Little Kittens'?
Fighting brings trouble; living together peacefully is better
The poem shows that quarrelling brings trouble, and living peacefully together is better.
The regular repeated pattern of sounds in a poem is called:
Rhythm is the regular repeated pattern of sounds.
